summary.headline: Ahead of target this week, but the quarter and year remain behind, with rising cancellations a growing risk.

points.what: Orders and revenue were both ahead of target this week, at 100.7% and 101.1% respectively, and both flagged notable for falling outside the normal 8-week range.
points.so_what: This means the week's outperformance sits outside the typical growth pattern seen in recent weeks.

points.what: QTD revenue attainment is 98.4%, a gap of -$8,518 against target.
points.so_what: The quarter remains behind target, and the year-to-date position is behind as well, despite this week's ahead-of-target result.

points.what: Cancellation rate rose to 15.8%, up 2.0 pp WoW, flagged notable for crossing the 1.0 pp threshold.
points.so_what: This is the main risk to watch this week.

points.what: Search was the largest contributor to order growth, accounting for 43.8% of the week's change.
points.so_what: Growth continues to concentrate in the channel that already holds the majority of orders.

points.what: Cancellation rate rose to 15.8%, up 2.0 pp WoW and up 2.8 pp YoY, both rated bad.
points.so_what: Each percentage point of cancellation equates to $850 in revenue, so this rise is a meaningful revenue risk this week.

points.what: YTD revenue attainment is 95.2%, with the required weekly run-rate of $82,530 above the current 8-week run-rate of $65,973.
points.so_what: At the current pace, the full-year target is not being closed.

points.what: New signups fell to 225, down 7.0% WoW, while orders grew 9.0% WoW over the same week.
points.so_what: Order growth this week did not come from more new signups, a risk if the trend continues.

points.what: Weekly orders were 100.7% of target and weekly revenue was 101.1% of target.
points.so_what: The week itself was ahead of target on both measures.

points.what: QTD revenue attainment is 98.4%, a gap of -$8,518 versus the target to date.
points.so_what: The quarter remains behind target even after this week's ahead-of-target result.

points.what: YTD revenue attainment is 95.2%, with a required weekly run-rate of $82,530 versus the current 8-week run-rate of $65,973.
points.so_what: The recent pace runs below what's required, so closing the year-end gap needs a faster pace than seen recently.

points.what: APAC contributed 28 orders and 35% of the week's order change, with orders up 6.9% WoW.
points.so_what: APAC was the single largest regional driver of this week's order growth.

points.what: Search contributed 35 orders and 43.8% of the week's order change, with orders up 5.6% WoW.
points.so_what: Search remains the largest driver of order growth, consistent with its already dominant share of orders.

points.what: Facebook contributed 25 orders and 31.2% of the week's order change, with orders up 61.0% WoW.
points.so_what: Despite the high percentage growth, Facebook contributed less to total order growth than Search or APAC.

points.what: AOV was $87.74, down 1.7% WoW but up 3.4% YoY.
points.so_what: The WoW dip means this week's revenue growth came more from additional orders than from higher spend per order.

points.what: The 14-Day Return Rate for the week of 04 May 2026 was 9.9%, down 0.2 pp WoW and flat YoY.
points.so_what: Returns are easing rather than adding to order-quality risk this week.

points.what: New signups were 225, down 7.0% WoW but up 6.1% YoY.
points.so_what: Signup growth of 6.1% YoY trails order growth's 88.5% YoY, a gap to monitor alongside the order trend.

checks.name: 14-Day Return Rate names its mature week
anomaly flag acknowledged in the summary
sentences at most 30 words and 4 numbers
each slot only covers its allowed KPIs
